1	"""Parameter extraction: fit SiPhon models to measured transmission spectra.
2	
3	Wraps :func:`scipy.optimize.least_squares` around any SiPhon S-parameter
4	model or :class:`siphon.circuit.Circuit`, so measured wafer-probe spectra
5	can calibrate model parameters (coupling, loss, effective/group index).
6	
7	How it works
8	------------
9	You supply a ``build(**params)`` callable that constructs the model from a
10	flat dict of floats, an initial guess ``params0``, and measured data on a
11	wavelength grid. The fitter minimizes the residual between the model's
12	named ``inport -> outport`` transmission and the data, in one of two
13	domains:
14	
15	* ``"power_db"``  — residual in 10*log10(|S|^2) dB (the natural domain for
16	  detector/OSA power traces; model power is floored at 1e-16, i.e. -160 dB,
17	  so exact model nulls stay finite).
18	* ``"field_mag"`` — residual in |S| (linear field magnitude).
19	
20	Only magnitude information is fit — measured phase is rarely available from
21	a power sweep. Parameters that enter only through phase offsets common to
22	all wavelengths are therefore invisible to the fit.
23	
24	Honesty limits
25	--------------
26	This is architecture-level extraction, not metrology signoff:
27	
28	* Local optimizer. ``least_squares`` converges to the nearest local
29	  minimum; resonant spectra (rings, MZIs) are violently multimodal in the
30	  index parameters, so ``params0`` must place the resonance comb within
31	  roughly half a free spectral range of the data. :func:`fit_ring_add_drop`
32	  mitigates this with a coarse scan over one resonance order of ``neff0``.
33	* Identifiability is the user's problem. Classic degeneracies survive any
34	  optimizer: a ring's ``neff0`` is only determined modulo the resonance
35	  order (shifts of wl0/L leave the comb almost unchanged); ``ng`` needs
36	  more than one FSR in the data; symmetric add-drop rings cannot separate
37	  kappa1 from kappa2 from the through port alone; loss and coupling trade
38	  off near critical coupling unless through AND drop are fit jointly.
39	* No measurement-system model. Fiber-coupling ripple, polarization drift,
40	  and detector nonlinearity must be de-embedded before fitting.
41	
42	Units: wavelengths um; power ratios in dB where suffixed ``_db``;
43	``residual_rms_db`` is in the units of the chosen domain (dB for
44	``power_db``, dimensionless field magnitude for ``field_mag``).
45	"""
46	
47	from __future__ import annotations
48	
49	from dataclasses import dataclass
50	from typing import Callable, Mapping
51	
52	import numpy as np
53	from scipy.optimize import least_squares
54	
55	from .components import RingAddDrop
56	
57	# Model power floor when converting to dB: exact transmission nulls (e.g. a
58	# critically coupled ring on resonance) map to -160 dB instead of -inf.
59	_POWER_FLOOR = 1e-16
60	
61	_DOMAINS = ("power_db", "field_mag")
62	
63	
64	# --- result container -------------------------------------------------------
65	
66	
67	@dataclass(frozen=True)
68	class FitResult:
69	    """Outcome of a least-squares parameter extraction.
70	
71	    Attributes
72	    ----------
73	    params : fitted parameter values, same keys as ``params0``.
74	    cost : final least-squares cost, 0.5 * sum(residual**2) (scipy's
75	        convention), in the square of the fit domain's units.
76	    residual_rms_db : root-mean-square residual over all fitted points, in
77	        the fit domain's units (dB for ``power_db``; despite the ``_db``
78	        suffix it is linear field magnitude for ``field_mag``). For a good
79	        fit this approaches the measurement noise floor.
80	    success : scipy convergence flag (a termination criterion was met).
81	    nfev : number of model evaluations.
82	    message : scipy termination message.
83	    """
84	
85	    params: dict[str, float]
86	    cost: float
87	    residual_rms_db: float
88	    success: bool
89	    nfev: int
90	    message: str
91	
92	    def report(self) -> str:
93	        """Multi-line human-readable summary of the fit."""
94	        lines = [
95	            f"FitResult: success={self.success}, nfev={self.nfev}",
96	            f"  cost = {self.cost:.6g}, residual rms = "
97	            f"{self.residual_rms_db:.4g} (fit-domain units)",
98	            f"  message: {self.message}",
99	            "  parameters:",
100	        ]
101	        width = max(len(k) for k in self.params)
102	        for key, value in self.params.items():
103	            lines.append(f"    {key.ljust(width)} = {value:.8g}")
104	        return "\n".join(lines)
105	
106	
107	# --- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------
108	
109	
110	def _wl_grid(wl_um) -> np.ndarray:
111	    wl = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(wl_um, dtype=float))
112	    if wl.ndim != 1 or wl.size < 2:
113	        raise ValueError("wl_um must be a 1-D array with at least 2 points")
114	    if np.any(wl <= 0):
115	        raise ValueError("wl_um must be positive (in um)")
116	    return wl
117	
118	
119	def _model_transmission(model, wl: np.ndarray, inport: str, outport: str) -> np.ndarray:
120	    """Complex inport->outport transmission of a component model or Circuit.
121	
122	    A Circuit is recognized by its ``transmission`` method and
123	    ``external_ports``; anything else must follow the component protocol
124	    (``ports`` tuple + ``s_params(wl)``). Raises ValueError for unknown
125	    port names.
126	    """
127	    if hasattr(model, "transmission") and hasattr(model, "external_ports"):
128	        known = model.external_ports
129	        for name in (inport, outport):
130	            if name not in known:
131	                raise ValueError(
132	                    f"unknown external port {name!r}; circuit exposes {known}"
133	                )
134	        return np.asarray(model.transmission(wl, inport, outport))
135	    ports = getattr(model, "ports", None)
136	    if not ports or not hasattr(model, "s_params"):
137	        raise TypeError(
138	            "build() must return a Circuit or a model exposing "
139	            "'ports' and 's_params(wl)'"
140	        )
141	    for name in (inport, outport):
142	        if name not in ports:
143	            raise ValueError(f"unknown port {name!r}; model ports are {ports}")
144	    s = np.asarray(model.s_params(wl))
145	    return s[:, ports.index(outport), ports.index(inport)]
146	
147	
148	def _to_domain(t: np.ndarray, domain: str) -> np.ndarray:
149	    """Complex transmission -> fit-domain observable (see module docstring)."""
150	    if domain == "power_db":
151	        return 10.0 * np.log10(np.maximum(np.abs(t) ** 2, _POWER_FLOOR))
152	    return np.abs(t)
153	
154	
155	def _normalize_paths(
156	    measured, inport, outport, n_wl: int
157	) -> list[tuple[str, str, np.ndarray]]:
158	    """Validate measured data into a list of (inport, outport, array)."""
159	    if isinstance(measured, Mapping):
160	        if inport is not None or outport is not None:
161	            raise ValueError(
162	                "when measured is a dict {(inport, outport): array}, do not "
163	                "also pass inport/outport"
164	            )
165	        if not measured:
166	            raise ValueError("measured dict is empty")
167	        paths = []
168	        for key, data in measured.items():
169	            if not (isinstance(key, tuple) and len(key) == 2):
170	                raise ValueError(
171	                    f"measured dict keys must be (inport, outport) tuples; got {key!r}"
172	                )
173	            paths.append((key[0], key[1], np.asarray(data, dtype=float)))
174	    else:
175	        if inport is None or outport is None:
176	            raise ValueError(
177	                "inport and outport are required when measured is a single array"
178	            )
179	        paths = [(inport, outport, np.asarray(measured, dtype=float))]
180	    for pin, pout, data in paths:
181	        if data.shape != (n_wl,):
182	            raise ValueError(
183	                f"measured data for ({pin!r}, {pout!r}) has shape {data.shape}; "
184	                f"expected ({n_wl},) matching wl_um"
185	            )
186	        if not np.all(np.isfinite(data)):
187	            raise ValueError(
188	                f"measured data for ({pin!r}, {pout!r}) contains non-finite values"
189	            )
190	    return paths
191	
192	
193	def _pack_bounds(
194	    names: list[str],
195	    params0: dict[str, float],
196	    bounds: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] | None,
197	) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
198	    """Bounds dict -> (lb, ub) vectors in ``names`` order, validated."""
199	    lb = np.full(len(names), -np.inf)
200	    ub = np.full(len(names), np.inf)
201	    if bounds is None:
202	        return lb, ub
203	    unknown = set(bounds) - set(names)
204	    if unknown:
205	        raise ValueError(
206	            f"bounds given for parameters not in params0: {sorted(unknown)}"
207	        )
208	    for i, name in enumerate(names):
209	        if name not in bounds:
210	            continue
211	        lo, hi = bounds[name]
212	        if not lo < hi:
213	            raise ValueError(f"bounds for {name!r} must satisfy lo < hi; got ({lo}, {hi})")
214	        if not lo <= params0[name] <= hi:
215	            raise ValueError(
216	                f"params0[{name!r}] = {params0[name]} lies outside bounds ({lo}, {hi})"
217	            )
218	        lb[i], ub[i] = lo, hi
219	    return lb, ub
220	
221	
222	# --- generic fitter ----------------------------------------------------------
223	
224	
225	def fit_transmission(
226	    build: Callable[..., object],
227	    params0: dict[str, float],
228	    wl_um,
229	    measured,
230	    *,
231	    inport: str | None = None,
232	    outport: str | None = None,
233	    bounds: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] | None = None,
234	    domain: str = "power_db",
235	    **fixed,
236	) -> FitResult:
237	    """Fit a model's free parameters to measured transmission spectra.
238	
239	    Minimizes sum over wavelengths (and paths) of
240	    ``(model_observable - measured)**2`` with
241	    :func:`scipy.optimize.least_squares` (trust-region reflective), where
242	    the observable is ``10*log10(|S_out,in|^2)`` for ``domain="power_db"``
243	    or ``|S_out,in|`` for ``domain="field_mag"``.
244	
245	    Parameters
246	    ----------
247	    build : callable; ``build(**{**fixed, **params})`` must return either a
248	        component model (``ports`` + ``s_params(wl)``) or a
249	        :class:`siphon.circuit.Circuit`.
250	    params0 : initial guess for the FREE parameters, dict of floats. Key
251	        order sets the internal parameter vector order.
252	    wl_um : 1-D wavelength grid in um (>= 2 points).
253	    measured : either a single array matching ``wl_um`` (then ``inport``
254	        and ``outport`` are required), or a dict
255	        ``{(inport, outport): array}`` to fit several paths jointly (then
256	        ``inport``/``outport`` must be omitted). Values are in the chosen
257	        domain's units (dB for ``power_db``, |S| for ``field_mag``).
258	    inport, outport : port names for the single-array form. For a
259	        component these are entries of ``model.ports``; for a Circuit,
260	        exposed external port names.
261	    bounds : optional ``{name: (lo, hi)}``; keys must be a subset of
262	        ``params0``; missing names are unbounded. ``params0`` must lie
263	        within its bounds.
264	    domain : ``"power_db"`` (default) or ``"field_mag"``.
265	    **fixed : extra keyword arguments passed to ``build`` unchanged (fixed,
266	        not fitted). Keys must not collide with ``params0``.
267	
268	    Returns
269	    -------
270	    FitResult with fitted params (same keys as ``params0``).
271	
272	    Raises
273	    ------
274	    ValueError on empty/non-finite ``params0``, bad domain, shape
275	    mismatches, unknown ports, bounds/params0/fixed key mismatches.
276	
277	    Notes
278	    -----
279	    Local optimization only — see the module docstring for the honesty
280	    limits (multimodality of resonant spectra, identifiability).
281	    """
282	    if domain not in _DOMAINS:
283	        raise ValueError(f"domain must be one of {_DOMAINS}; got {domain!r}")
284	    if not params0:
285	        raise ValueError("params0 must contain at least one free parameter")
286	    for key, value in params0.items():
287	        if not np.isfinite(value):
288	            raise ValueError(f"params0[{key!r}] = {value} is not finite")
289	    overlap = set(params0) & set(fixed)
290	    if overlap:
291	        raise ValueError(
292	            f"parameters appear in both params0 and fixed kwargs: {sorted(overlap)}"
293	        )
294	
295	    wl = _wl_grid(wl_um)
296	    paths = _normalize_paths(measured, inport, outport, wl.size)
297	    names = list(params0)
298	    x0 = np.array([params0[k] for k in names], dtype=float)
299	    lb, ub = _pack_bounds(names, params0, bounds)
300	
301	    # Fail fast (with a clean ValueError) on unknown ports / bad build.
302	    model0 = build(**{**fixed, **params0})
303	    for pin, pout, _ in paths:
304	        _model_transmission(model0, wl, pin, pout)
305	
306	    def residual(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
307	        params = dict(zip(names, x))
308	        model = build(**{**fixed, **params})
309	        parts = [
310	            _to_domain(_model_transmission(model, wl, pin, pout), domain) - data
311	            for pin, pout, data in paths
312	        ]
313	        return np.concatenate(parts)
314	
315	    # x_scale="jac": rescale parameters by Jacobian column norms, so kappas
316	    # (~1e-2) and indices (~1) converge together instead of stalling on xtol.
317	    res = least_squares(residual, x0, bounds=(lb, ub), method="trf", x_scale="jac")
318	    rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(res.fun**2)))
319	    return FitResult(
320	        params={k: float(v) for k, v in zip(names, res.x)},
321	        cost=float(res.cost),
322	        residual_rms_db=rms,
323	        success=bool(res.success),
324	        nfev=int(res.nfev),
325	        message=str(res.message),
326	    )
327	
328	
329	# --- ring add-drop convenience ------------------------------------------------
330	
331	
332	_RING_FREE = ("kappa1_power", "kappa2_power", "loss_db_per_cm", "neff0", "ng")
333	
334	_RING_X0 = {
335	    "kappa1_power": 0.1,
336	    "kappa2_power": 0.1,
337	    "loss_db_per_cm": 2.0,
338	    "neff0": 2.4,
339	    "ng": 4.2,
340	}
341	
342	_RING_BOUNDS = {
343	    "kappa1_power": (1e-4, 0.9),
344	    "kappa2_power": (1e-4, 0.9),
345	    "loss_db_per_cm": (0.0, 1e3),
346	    "neff0": (1.0, 4.5),
347	    "ng": (1.0, 8.0),
348	}
349	
350	
351	def fit_ring_add_drop(
352	    wl_um,
353	    through_db,
354	    drop_db,
355	    x0: dict | None = None,
356	    *,
357	    circumference_um: float,
358	    wl0_um: float = 1.55,
359	    bounds: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] | None = None,
360	) -> FitResult:
361	    """Fit a :class:`siphon.components.RingAddDrop` to through+drop spectra.
362	
363	    Jointly fits (kappa1_power, kappa2_power, loss_db_per_cm, neff0, ng)
364	    to the measured in->through and in->drop power spectra in dB, via
365	    :func:`fit_transmission`. The joint fit is what breaks the
366	    loss-vs-coupling degeneracy: through-port extinction and drop-port
367	    insertion loss constrain different combinations of (kappa1, kappa2, a).
368	
369	    Before the least-squares run, ``neff0`` is coarsely scanned over one
370	    resonance-order spacing (wl0/L, 61 samples) about its initial guess and
371	    the best offset is kept, so the resonance comb starts aligned with the
372	    data — this is what makes the local optimizer land in the right basin.
373	
374	    Parameters
375	    ----------
376	    wl_um : 1-D wavelength grid in um; SHOULD span several FSRs (see below).
377	    through_db, drop_db : measured power transmission in dB, same shape as
378	        ``wl_um``.
379	    x0 : optional initial-guess overrides for any of the five free
380	        parameters (unknown keys raise ValueError). Defaults: kappas 0.1,
381	        loss 2 dB/cm, neff0 2.4, ng 4.2 — supply design values whenever
382	        you have them; the coarse neff0 scan only searches one resonance
383	        order around the guess.
384	    circumference_um : ring round-trip length in um, FIXED from layout.
385	        It is not fittable: only the products neff0*L and ng*L enter the
386	        response, so L and the indices are exactly degenerate.
387	    wl0_um : dispersion expansion wavelength passed to RingAddDrop; pick it
388	        inside the measured span.
389	    bounds : optional per-parameter overrides of the defaults
390	        (kappas in (1e-4, 0.9), loss in (0, 1000) dB/cm, neff0 in
391	        (1.0, 4.5), ng in (1.0, 8.0)).
392	
393	    Returns
394	    -------
395	    FitResult over the five free parameters; ``residual_rms_db`` is the rms
396	    misfit in dB over both spectra.
397	
398	    Identifiability — read before trusting the numbers
399	    --------------------------------------------------
400	    * ``neff0`` is identifiable only modulo the resonance order: adding any
401	      integer multiple of ~wl0/L to neff0 shifts the comb by whole orders
402	      and reproduces (almost) the same spectrum. The returned value is the
403	      one nearest the initial guess; report it as "neff0 assuming order m".
404	    * ``ng`` is constrained by the FSR, so the data must contain more than
405	      one FSR; spanning 3+ FSRs is recommended (with a single resonance in
406	      view, ng returns the initial guess dressed in noise).
407	    * ``kappa1``/``kappa2``/``loss``: a correlated (kappa1 down, kappa2 up,
408	      loss up) direction changes the magnitude spectra by only ~0.1 dB per
409	      ~10% parameter shift near the through-port dip — flat at typical
410	      probe-noise levels (0.05 dB rms), so several parameter sets fit the
411	      data equally well. The optimizer returns the valley point nearest
412	      ``x0``: start from the intended DESIGN asymmetry (kappa1 vs kappa2)
413	      and treat the split with ~10% uncertainty unless the noise floor is
414	      well below 0.05 dB or phase/group-delay data is added.
415	    * Coupler excess loss is not modeled; it is absorbed into
416	      loss_db_per_cm.
417	    """
418	    wl = _wl_grid(wl_um)
419	    if circumference_um <= 0:
420	        raise ValueError("circumference_um must be positive")
421	
422	    params0 = dict(_RING_X0)
423	    if x0:
424	        unknown = set(x0) - set(_RING_FREE)
425	        if unknown:
426	            raise ValueError(
427	                f"x0 keys must be among {_RING_FREE}; unknown: {sorted(unknown)}"
428	            )
429	        params0.update({k: float(v) for k, v in x0.items()})
430	
431	    eff_bounds = dict(_RING_BOUNDS)
432	    if bounds:
433	        unknown = set(bounds) - set(_RING_FREE)
434	        if unknown:
435	            raise ValueError(
436	                f"bounds keys must be among {_RING_FREE}; unknown: {sorted(unknown)}"
437	            )
438	        eff_bounds.update(bounds)
439	
440	    measured = {
441	        ("in", "through"): np.asarray(through_db, dtype=float),
442	        ("in", "drop"): np.asarray(drop_db, dtype=float),
443	    }
444	
445	    def build(**p) -> RingAddDrop:
446	        return RingAddDrop(**p)
447	
448	    fixed = {"circumference_um": circumference_um, "wl0_um": wl0_um}
449	
450	    # Coarse neff0 scan over one resonance-order spacing to align the comb.
451	    paths = _normalize_paths(measured, None, None, wl.size)
452	    order_spacing = wl0_um / circumference_um
453	    lo, hi = eff_bounds["neff0"]
454	    best_neff0, best_sse = params0["neff0"], np.inf
455	    for offset in np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 61) * order_spacing:
456	        neff0 = params0["neff0"] + offset
457	        if not lo <= neff0 <= hi:
458	            continue
459	        model = build(**{**fixed, **params0, "neff0": neff0})
460	        sse = 0.0
461	        for pin, pout, data in paths:
462	            obs = _to_domain(_model_transmission(model, wl, pin, pout), "power_db")
463	            sse += float(np.sum((obs - data) ** 2))
464	        if sse < best_sse:
465	            best_neff0, best_sse = neff0, sse
466	    params0["neff0"] = best_neff0
467	
468	    return fit_transmission(
469	        build,
470	        params0,
471	        wl,
472	        measured,
473	        bounds=eff_bounds,
474	        domain="power_db",
475	        **fixed,
476	    )

2	"""SiPhon example 05 — parameter extraction from a wafer probe trace.
3	
4	Pretends a probe station measured the through- and drop-port power spectra
5	of an add-drop microring (synthesized here from known ground truth plus
6	0.05 dB rms Gaussian noise, spanning ~3 FSRs), then calibrates a
7	RingAddDrop model to the trace with siphon.extract.fit_ring_add_drop. The
8	script prints a true-vs-recovered parameter table with the fit's residual
9	rms against the injected noise floor, and saves an overlay plot (measured
10	points, fitted curves, residuals) to examples/out/.
11	
12	The fit is architecture-level model calibration, not metrology: neff0 is
13	recovered only modulo the resonance order (the circumference is fixed from
14	layout), and ng is only identifiable because the trace spans several FSRs.
15	
16	Units: um for wavelength/geometry, dB for transmission, dB/cm for loss.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	from pathlib import Path
22	
23	import numpy as np
24	
25	# Design/ground truth ------------------------------------------------------
26	CIRC_UM = 200.0          # ring circumference, known from layout (fixed in fit)
27	WL0_UM = 1.55            # dispersion expansion wavelength
28	TRUE = {
29	    "kappa1_power": 0.08,
30	    "kappa2_power": 0.06,
31	    "loss_db_per_cm": 3.0,
32	    "neff0": 2.35,
33	    "ng": 4.1,
34	}
35	NOISE_DB = 0.05          # probe-trace noise, dB rms
36	SEED = 7
37	
38	# Chart palette (validated categorical slots, light mode)
39	SERIES = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834"]      # through, drop
40	SURFACE = "#fcfcfb"
41	INK = "#0b0b0b"
42	INK_2 = "#52514e"
43	GRID = "#e5e4e0"
44	
45	
46	def header(title: str) -> None:
47	    print()

54	    print("  ".join(h.rjust(w) for h, w in zip(headers, widths)))

60	def synthesize_probe_trace(RingAddDrop):
61	    """Noisy through/drop dB spectra over ~3 FSRs of the ground-truth ring."""
62	    fsr_um = WL0_UM**2 / (TRUE["ng"] * CIRC_UM)          # FSR = wl^2/(ng L)
63	    span = 3.05 * fsr_um
64	    wl = np.linspace(WL0_UM - span / 2, WL0_UM + span / 2, 1501)
65	    ring = RingAddDrop(circumference_um=CIRC_UM, wl0_um=WL0_UM, **TRUE)
66	    s = ring.s_params(wl)
67	    i_in = ring.ports.index("in")
68	    thru_db = 10 * np.log10(np.abs(s[:, ring.ports.index("through"), i_in]) ** 2)
69	    drop_db = 10 * np.log10(np.abs(s[:, ring.ports.index("drop"), i_in]) ** 2)
70	    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
71	    thru_db = thru_db + rng.normal(0.0, NOISE_DB, wl.size)
72	    drop_db = drop_db + rng.normal(0.0, NOISE_DB, wl.size)
73	    return wl, thru_db, drop_db, fsr_um

76	def model_spectra_db(RingAddDrop, params, wl):
77	    ring = RingAddDrop(circumference_um=CIRC_UM, wl0_um=WL0_UM, **params)
78	    s = ring.s_params(wl)
79	    thru = 10 * np.log10(np.maximum(np.abs(s[:, 1, 0]) ** 2, 1e-16))
80	    drop = 10 * np.log10(np.maximum(np.abs(s[:, 3, 0]) ** 2, 1e-16))
81	    return thru, drop

101	    )

109	    # measured points (subsampled so the markers stay readable) + fitted lines

112	        (thru_db, fit_thru, SERIES[0], "through"),
113	        (drop_db, fit_drop, SERIES[1], "drop"),

6	``s_params(wl: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray`` of shape

13	  consistently for ALL models. Ring transfer functions follow Bogaerts et

15	  conjugated to ``exp(-1j*phi)`` — Bogaerts writes ``e^{+i phi}`` under the
16	  physics ``e^{-i omega t}`` convention, and using it unconjugated next to

18	  interferometric composition in :class:`siphon.circuit.Circuit`. Magnitudes,

23	  unitary as a 3-port).

25	  ``n_eff(wl) = neff0 + (wl - wl0) * (neff0 - ng) / wl0``,
26	  which follows from ``n_g = n_eff - wl * d(n_eff)/d(wl)``. Valid over

1	"""Frequency-domain S-parameter circuit solver.
2	
3	Assembles a netlist of S-parameter models into a single external S-matrix by
4	eliminating internal (connected) ports, the standard multiport interconnection
5	method (Filipsson 1981; also known as subnetwork growth). Per wavelength the
6	block-diagonal S of all instances is partitioned into external (e) and
7	internal (i) ports; with P the permutation exchanging each connected pair
8	(a_i = P b_i),
9	
10	    S_ext = S_ee + S_ei P (I - S_ii P)^-1 S_ie.
11	
12	Model protocol: a model exposes ``ports: tuple[str, ...]`` and
13	``s_params(wl) -> ndarray`` of shape ``(len(wl), n, n)``, complex, with
14	b_p = sum_q S[k, p, q] a_q at vacuum wavelength ``wl[k]`` in um. Port order in
15	the matrix equals the order of ``ports``.
16	
17	Validity: linear, time-invariant, single-mode-per-port networks only. A
18	lossless feedback loop exactly on resonance makes (I - S_ii P) singular — the
19	physical steady state does not exist — and raises rather than returning noise.
20	
21	Conventions: wavelengths in um; ``transmission_db`` returns power dB.
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	import numpy as np
27	
28	# Condition number of (I - S_ii P) above which the internal solve is treated
29	# as singular (resonant lossless loop, or a model with gain >= loop loss).
30	_COND_LIMIT = 1e12
31	
32	Port = tuple[str, str]  # (instance name, port name)
33	
34	
35	class Circuit:
36	    """Netlist of S-parameter model instances solved to one external S-matrix.
37	
38	    Build with :meth:`add`, wire with :meth:`connect`, name outside-world
39	    ports with :meth:`expose`, then call :meth:`s_params`. External port
40	    order in the result is the order of the ``expose`` calls.
41	    """
42	
43	    def __init__(self) -> None:
44	        self._instances: dict[str, object] = {}
45	        self._connections: list[tuple[Port, Port]] = []
46	        self._exposed: dict[str, Port] = {}
47	        self._used_ports: set[Port] = set()
48	
49	    # --- construction ------------------------------------------------------
50	
51	    def add(self, name: str, model) -> None:
52	        """Register a model instance under a unique name."""
53	        if name in self._instances:
54	            raise ValueError(f"instance {name!r} already added")
55	        ports = getattr(model, "ports", None)
56	        if not ports or not hasattr(model, "s_params"):
57	            raise TypeError(
58	                f"model for {name!r} must expose 'ports' and 's_params(wl)'"
59	            )
60	        if len(set(ports)) != len(ports):
61	            raise ValueError(f"model for {name!r} has duplicate port names: {ports}")
62	        self._instances[name] = model
63	
64	    def connect(self, a: Port, b: Port) -> None:
65	        """Join two instance ports. Each port may be used at most once."""
66	        self._resolve(a)
67	        self._resolve(b)
68	        if a == b:
69	            raise ValueError(f"cannot connect port {a} to itself")
70	        for port in (a, b):
71	            if port in self._used_ports:
72	                raise ValueError(f"port {port} is already connected or exposed")
73	        self._connections.append((a, b))
74	        self._used_ports.update((a, b))
75	
76	    def expose(self, external_name: str, port: Port) -> None:
77	        """Make an instance port an external port named ``external_name``."""
78	        self._resolve(port)
79	        if external_name in self._exposed:
80	            raise ValueError(f"external port {external_name!r} already defined")
81	        if port in self._used_ports:
82	            raise ValueError(f"port {port} is already connected or exposed")
83	        self._exposed[external_name] = port
84	        self._used_ports.add(port)
85	
86	    @property
87	    def external_ports(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
88	        """External port names in expose() order (== S-matrix port order)."""
89	        return tuple(self._exposed)
90	
91	    def _resolve(self, port: Port) -> int:
92	        """Global port index of (instance, port); raises if unknown."""
93	        inst, pname = port
94	        if inst not in self._instances:
95	            raise KeyError(f"unknown instance {inst!r}; known: {sorted(self._instances)}")
96	        offset = 0
97	        for name, model in self._instances.items():
98	            if name == inst:
99	                break
100	            offset += len(model.ports)
101	        model = self._instances[inst]
102	        if pname not in model.ports:
103	            raise KeyError(
104	                f"instance {inst!r} has no port {pname!r}; ports: {model.ports}"
105	            )
106	        return offset + model.ports.index(pname)
107	
108	    # --- solve --------------------------------------------------------------
109	
110	    def s_params(self, wl: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
111	        """External S-matrix, shape (len(wl), n_ext, n_ext), wl in um.
112	
113	        Raises ValueError if any instance port is neither connected nor
114	        exposed, and numpy.linalg.LinAlgError if the internal solve is
115	        singular at some wavelength (lossless resonant loop).
116	        """
117	        wl = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(wl, dtype=float))
118	        if not self._instances:
119	            raise ValueError("circuit has no instances")
120	
121	        dangling = [
122	            (name, pname)
123	            for name, model in self._instances.items()
124	            for pname in model.ports
125	            if (name, pname) not in self._used_ports
126	        ]
127	        if dangling:
128	            raise ValueError(f"unconnected and unexposed ports: {dangling}")
129	
130	        n_total = sum(len(m.ports) for m in self._instances.values())
131	        s_block = np.zeros((len(wl), n_total, n_total), dtype=complex)
132	        offset = 0
133	        for name, model in self._instances.items():
134	            n = len(model.ports)
135	            sm = np.asarray(model.s_params(wl), dtype=complex)
136	            if sm.shape != (len(wl), n, n):
137	                raise ValueError(
138	                    f"instance {name!r}: s_params returned shape {sm.shape}, "
139	                    f"expected {(len(wl), n, n)}"
140	                )
141	            s_block[:, offset : offset + n, offset : offset + n] = sm
142	            offset += n
143	
144	        ext = np.array([self._resolve(p) for p in self._exposed.values()], dtype=int)
145	        internal_ports = [p for pair in self._connections for p in pair]
146	        internal = np.array([self._resolve(p) for p in internal_ports], dtype=int)
147	        n_i = len(internal)
148	
149	        # a_int = P b_int: each connected pair exchanges its waves.
150	        perm = np.zeros((n_i, n_i))
151	        for m in range(0, n_i, 2):
152	            perm[m, m + 1] = perm[m + 1, m] = 1.0
153	
154	        # All wavelengths solved as one stacked system (matmul, cond and
155	        # solve broadcast over the leading axis) — same math per slice as a
156	        # per-wavelength loop, order of magnitude faster on dense sweeps.
157	        s_ee = s_block[:, ext[:, None], ext[None, :]]
158	        if n_i == 0:
159	            return s_ee
160	        s_ei = s_block[:, ext[:, None], internal[None, :]]
161	        s_ie = s_block[:, internal[:, None], ext[None, :]]
162	        s_ii = s_block[:, internal[:, None], internal[None, :]]
163	        m_int = np.eye(n_i) - s_ii @ perm
164	        finite = np.isfinite(m_int).reshape(len(wl), -1).all(axis=1)
165	        if finite.all():
166	            bad = np.flatnonzero(np.linalg.cond(m_int) > _COND_LIMIT)
167	        else:
168	            bad = np.flatnonzero(~finite)
169	        if bad.size:
170	            k = int(bad[0])
171	            raise np.linalg.LinAlgError(
172	                f"singular internal network at wavelength index {k} "
173	                f"(wl = {wl[k]} um): lossless resonant loop or gain"
174	            )
175	        return s_ee + s_ei @ perm @ np.linalg.solve(m_int, s_ie)
176	
177	    # --- convenience ---------------------------------------------------------
178	
179	    def transmission(self, wl: np.ndarray, inport: str, outport: str) -> np.ndarray:
180	        """Complex field transmission b_out / a_in vs wavelength (um)."""
181	        for name in (inport, outport):
182	            if name not in self._exposed:
183	                raise KeyError(
184	                    f"unknown external port {name!r}; known: {self.external_ports}"
185	                )
186	        names = self.external_ports
187	        s = self.s_params(wl)
188	        return s[:, names.index(outport), names.index(inport)]
189	
190	    def transmission_db(self, wl: np.ndarray, inport: str, outport: str) -> np.ndarray:
191	        """Power transmission in dB (<= 0 for passive networks); -inf if zero."""
192	        t = self.transmission(wl, inport, outport)
193	        with np.errstate(divide="ignore"):
194	            return 10.0 * np.log10(np.abs(t) ** 2)

No fit result is returned. The library's own test for this component quietly passes bounds={'coupling': (1e-4, 0.999)} to avoid this; fit_ring_add_drop protects itself with _RING_BOUNDS, but the generic fit_transmission defaults lb/ub to +/-inf (line 199-200) while every component model validates its domain in __post_init__.
findings.suggested_fix: Document loudly in fit_transmission that domain-constrained parameters (couplings, kappas, losses) must be given bounds, and/or catch ValueError from build() inside residual() and re-raise with a message naming the offending trial parameter values and suggesting bounds.
